## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Iddhibalakathā* (Kv 11.5) is a debate located in the eleventh chapter (*vagga*) of the Abhidhamma treatise *Kathāvatthu* [SuttaCentral]. The controversy examines the proposition of whether an individual endowed with psychic or supernormal power (*iddhibala*) can survive or remain for an entire cosmic age (*kappa*) [Bareau 1955; La Vallée Poussin, Conciles bouddhiques]. While scriptural passages record the Buddha stating that one who has developed and mastered the four bases of psychic power (*iddhipāda*) could remain for a *kappa* if desired, the orthodox Theravāda argument counters that lifespan (*āyu*), destiny (*gati*), and personality are not created by *iddhi*; psychic force cannot render conditioned aggregates (*khandha*) permanent (*nicca*) or prevent mortal and aging phenomena from dying and decaying [Bareau 1955; La Vallée Poussin, Conciles bouddhiques]. Louis de La Vallée Poussin notes that this debate emerged early in Buddhist dogmatics to harmonize scriptural statements regarding life-prolonging psychic powers with the doctrine of universal impermanence [La Vallée Poussin, Conciles bouddhiques].
SuttaCentral notes connections between this discussion and several canonical and paracanonical texts, including the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16), the *Cetiyasutta* (SN 51.10), the *Āyusaṅkhārossajjana Sutta* (Ud 6.1), the *Pāṭibhogasutta* (AN 4.182), the *Bhūmicālasutta* (AN 8.70), Chinese parallels (MĀ 36 and EĀ 42.5), and two passages in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.1.4 and Mil 5.1.10) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects significant Pali-internal text reuse with the *Catukkanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (specifically matching AN 4.182 at segments 7.4–7.10) and the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16 §6.5 matching DN 16 §3.43–3.44), where SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus agree [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records substantial internal reuse with related *Kathāvatthu* sections—including *Aparāpisamannāgatakathā* (Kv 4.9), *Iddhikathā* (Kv 21.4), and *Kappaṭṭhakathā* (Kv 13.1)—as well as the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*, and cross-language alignments with Tibetan versions of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sutta* and the *Śatasāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā* [DharmaNexus]. One modern translation is listed on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
